Hi Sofia — thanks for the note and the context. Short answers up front, then a couple of options depending on how you want to structure the pilot. Attachment: Redwood_Hosted_RateCard_Q2_2026.pdf (rate card) and draft_MutualActionPlan_ACME-v1.docx (pilot MAP).

1) Minimums: We support pay-as-you-go (no minimum) for hosted API, but discounting is applied only when you take a commit. For pilots we often do a short commit to guarantee capacity and offset the onboarding work.

2) Typical commit tiers (hosted API):
   - Month-to-month (no commit): list pricing, no discount, billed monthly.
   - 3-month pilot commit (recommended for pilots): minimum $5k/mo equivalent (prepaid or invoiced), typically ~10-15% discount off list depending on usage profile.
   - 6-month commit: recommended for mid-size rollouts; starts around $25k/mo with 15-20% discount.
   - 12-month/annual: larger commits (e.g., $100k/mo) with 25-35% pricing leverage and priority capacity.

3) Flexibility & exit: For pilots we can offer a 30-day exit/opt-out in the 3-month plan with a limited unwind fee (pro-rated). For longer commits we usually require 60-day notice or a negotiated buyout.

4) Compliance & residency: We can provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and region pinning to us-east for hosted customers (standard enterprise add-on).

If you're interested in a constrained pilot, the typical approach we recommend is a 3-month $5k/mo commit with a 10% discount (applied as invoice credit), plus a MAP to define success metrics and a rollback clause. That keeps your upfront commitment small while guaranteeing capacity.

Would you like me to draft a short MSA addendum and pricing term sheet? I can also loop in sales engineering for latency numbers for your expected traffic.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
